What the platform shows, and what the ledger reconstructs.

Headline rates, leaderboard returns, and familiar tickers are only the visible layer. These three figures preview the evidence each module adds underneath.

Three modules
01 / Hidden Fees and Cost Opacity

Fees & Hidden Cost

Enter an amount, asset, platform and leverage. This reconstructs what spot margin interest and futures funding actually cost you over your holding period, adds trading fees, and shows the total as a share of your real capital — not the headline rate on the platform's homepage.

Open module↗
02 / Visible Performance and Hidden Risk

Copy-Trading Risk

A 4-point pre-copy checklist, followed by a simulator built on real history from 200 lead traders: raw index decline, whether the 7/30/90-day returns even agree with each other, and your real take-home after profit share.

Open module↗
03 / Tokenised Assets and Stablecoin Risk

Asset Lookup

Is what you're buying a perpetual future, a tokenised claim, or a synthetic derivative priced entirely at the platform's discretion? Check its on-chain verification record, its pricing-discretion tier, and how its quote compares to Hyperliquid.

Open module↗

Build a copy scenario

Scenario inputs

Trader names are replaced with researcher-assigned pseudonyms (e.g., "#017 Aster"); account IDs are not published.
Profit-share assumptions · editable
OKX's published rules set the lead trader's profit share at 8%–13% of net profit depending on trader tier (10% is the figure used in OKX's own worked example, so it's the default here), charged only when the copy position is profitable. OKX's help centre states no other transaction fee is charged beyond this share, which is why the platform cut defaults to 0%: OKX Lead Trader Profit-Sharing Rules
